sources.title: Al-Farabi's own surviving works, including The Virtuous City (Mabadi' Ara' Ahl al-Madina al-Fadila), the Book of Music (Kitab al-Musiqa al-Kabir), and his commentaries on Aristotelian logic
Later medieval Islamic biographical dictionaries (e.g. Ibn Abi Usaybi'a's history of physicians and scholars) recording his career and reputed teaching lineage
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, "al-Farabi's Philosophy of Logic and Language", quoting his own account preserved in Ibn Abi Usaybi'a

systems_abstraction.rationale: The Virtuous City constructs a complete, integrated political-philosophical system linking cosmology, human psychology, and ideal governance into one coherent framework, documented directly via the structure and content of the surviving text.

analytical_rigor.rationale: Wrote extensive, systematic commentaries on Aristotle's logical works (the Organon), earning the later honorific "the Second Teacher" (after Aristotle himself), documented via the surviving commentaries and their subsequent influence on later Islamic and European logic. [NEW_EVIDENCE, Roster32] A second, independent documented instance from his own Book of Music: he holds that musical principles derive from mathematics but explicitly treats the ear as the final arbiter when it conflicts with a clean ratio -- stating outright that a semitone is not exactly half a whole tone, letting observation override a tidier preferred model.

cross_domain_range.rationale: Produced substantive surviving work across logic, political philosophy, metaphysics, and music theory (the Book of Music is a major, technically detailed treatise on the physics and aesthetics of musical sound), inferred as genuine cross-domain range from the documented range of these distinct surviving works.

independent_thinking.rationale: Synthesized Platonic, Aristotelian, and Islamic theological concepts into his own distinct political philosophy of the "virtuous city" rather than simply transmitting Greek philosophy unchanged, inferred as independent synthesis from the documented content of the Virtuous City relative to its Greek sources.

curiosity.rationale: The range of his surviving corpus (logic, ethics, political theory, music, psychology) suggests wide intellectual engagement, inferred from the documented breadth of subjects addressed across his works.

mastery_orientation.rationale: Later biographical tradition records him studying logic intensively under multiple teachers before producing his own influential commentaries. [NEW_EVIDENCE, Roster32] Strengthened by his own (now-lost) self-account, preserved via Ibn Abi Usaybi'a: he describes studying Aristotle's Organon under Yuhanna ibn Haylan up through the Posterior Analytics within a specific inherited Alexandria-Antioch-Baghdad curriculum, and notes the material beyond that point was withheld under the school's own religious restrictions -- a specific, self-described account of his formation's institutional limits, not just a generic 'studied under teachers' characterization. Still capped in the inference band: this is one self-account transmitted almost three and a half centuries after his death.

autonomy_need.rationale: Later biographical tradition records him living a relatively modest, itinerant scholarly life across Baghdad, Damascus, and Aleppo rather than seeking a single settled court position, inferred as some real independence from institutional attachment, though the specific evidence for this pattern is comparatively thin.

detail_orientation.rationale: His logical commentaries include close, term-by-term analysis of Aristotelian categories and syllogistic forms, inferred as requiring exacting analytical detail from the documented structure of the surviving commentaries.

impact_motivation.rationale: The Virtuous City is explicitly framed as a practical guide toward a well-ordered, flourishing political community rather than pure abstract metaphysics, inferred as genuine broader-impact motivation from the documented, stated practical aim of the work.

provenance.notes: Roster-1000 session 12: West Asia diversity pick (region was at 1/87, Rumi alone, before this batch). Sourced primarily from his own surviving philosophical/musicological corpus plus later medieval Islamic biographical dictionaries -- administrative/scholarly-tradition tier evidence, similar to this project's existing treatment of other medieval Islamic scholars. Scored at 7 rows reflecting genuinely available evidence; attributes like risk_tolerance, collaboration, and social_assertiveness have no independently-documented basis for this specific person and were left unscored rather than padded. Scored under the corrected, eligibility-blind process. Roster32 (2026-09): a bounded NEW_EVIDENCE research pass explicitly probing for a Hippocrates-style attribution failure found the concern was warranted -- most personal-life anecdotes about Al-Farabi (a claimed modest stipend and declined court gifts, a court musical-performance story, temperament characterizations, even the specific circumstances of his death) trace to biographical dictionaries written 250-320+ years after he died, are sometimes internally contradictory across those dictionaries, and in one case (the Aleppo/Sayf al-Dawla patronage narrative) are entirely absent from the most philologically rigorous modern source consulted (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy). A modern peer-reviewed specialist (Pormann, JAOS 2015) is quoted concluding it is doubtful myth and reality can ever be fully separated for this figure. Only 2 rows were touched (analytical_rigor, mastery_orientation), both upgraded from his own surviving texts/self-account rather than from the later biographical tradition. See docs/checkpoints/roster32-evidence-deepening-balance-cycle.md for the full ledger, including the specific disputed-authorship finding on the 'Harmonization of Plato and Aristotle' treatise (deliberately not used as evidence of his own method pending that dispute's resolution).

holdReason: Roster32 evidence-deepening cycle: this candidate's evidentiary ceiling, not researcher effort, is the binding constraint. A full bounded research pass (9 sources, ~1 hour) found the reliable individually-attributed behavioral record for Al-Farabi is genuinely narrow -- his own surviving texts and one self-preserved training account -- while the bulk of personal-life texture in the wider tradition is late, thin, and in places disputed by the specialists who study it most closely. Correctly declined to score any of that shakier material rather than manufacture rows. Row count unchanged at 9 (2 rows upgraded); still far short of the 18-attribute floor. Held, not rejected -- this candidate is probably at or near its honest ceiling absent a genuinely new primary-source discovery, which is a different kind of finding than "needs more research effort."
